I like it a lot, but I didn't read Hellboy.

Apparently the cult of the black flame originates from the Hellboy series, but I don't think any of the lead characters in this story have any ties to Hellboy. Rise definately isn't a super hero, super powers, action based comic. It's a slow adventure from the civilized world to the jungle in search of missing girls, and the detectives discover a little more each issue about what is going on. The cult (Black Flame?) haven't made many appearances, as they are the mystery in the story.

What I am trying to say is if you go into it expecting Hellboy, you'll probably be disappointed. This is easy to understand, since the issues are marketed as "From the Pages of Hellboy!". If you go into it as a new comic series I think most people will be happy with it. I like the pacing a lot. As I mentioned above, the story is a slow burn, and the letterer did a fantastic job of keeping the reader from reading the book too fast. Word balloons are where they should be, and spaced properly for if something is happening quickly, or if the reader should also be taking in the art and movements between conversation. I know it's odd to compliment a books lettering, but I catch myself reading some books too fast due to bad layout, then going back and forcing myself to take a scene in again at the proper pacing after I figure it out.
